passage.title: Teacher-written report for TGA
paras: Living things pass on traits to their offspring. A trait is a feature, such as the colour of a flower or the shape of a seed.
In the 1850s and 1860s, a monk called Gregor Mendel grew thousands of pea plants. He noticed that traits such as flower colour and seed shape were passed on in patterns.
Today we know that traits are carried by genes. Offspring receive genes from both parents, which is why they are similar to, but never exactly the same as, either one.
